response.content:
## Health Tech Companies Entering the Swedish Market in 2026

The Swedish health tech ecosystem is vibrant, with approximately **1,164 health tech companies** operating in the country and **20 new health tech startups founded in Sweden so far in 2026**. Sweden ranks **#8 globally** for health tech, with an estimated ecosystem value of **US $13 billion**. Here are the key developments regarding health tech market entries and expansions in Sweden during 2026:

### Notable Market Entries & Expansions

- **Neko Health** — Co-founded by Spotify CEO Daniel Ek and entrepreneur Hjalmar Nilsonne, this Swedish AI-powered preventive body-scanning company has been expanding rapidly. Originally launched in Stockholm in 2023, it expanded to the UK in 2024 and opened its first US clinic in New York City in September 2026. It raised a **Series C round** in July 2026 with investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners and 24 others. Neko continues to hire actively in Stockholm.

- **Kry** — The European digital and physical primary care provider expanded its Swedish footprint significantly in 2026 by acquiring **Medinord** and agreeing to acquire **Min Doktor**, a Swedish healthcare provider part-owned by pharmacy chain Apotek Hjärtat. Since 2020, Kry has acquired numerous Swedish healthcare providers including Helsa, PBM, Cityläkarna, and others.

- **Tandem Health** — A Stockholm-based health tech company building AI to reduce administrative burden in healthcare, raised a **Series B round** in September 2026 backed by Scaleup Europe Fund and four other investors. The company is actively hiring for commercial roles in Sweden.

- **AMRA Medical** (Linköping, Sweden) — Raised a **Series A round** in September 2026 from Healthcap.

- **Eyedentity AI** (Stockholm) — Raised a **Seed round** in August 2026 from Norrsken Launcher.

- **Omaia** — A Swedish AI health tech startup that raised a **Seed round** in May 2026.

- **CareifAI** — Mentioned among new Swedish health tech startups emerging in mid-2026.

### Norwegian Health Tech Companies Eyeing Sweden

Norway Health Tech, Norway's largest health technology ecosystem, organized events in 2026 specifically focused on helping Norwegian digital health companies enter or establish themselves in the Swedish market, exploring the Swedish IT landscape, interoperability, data sharing, and market access.

### Broader Market Context

- Sweden's eHealth Agency has been calling for stronger national oversight and common standards for healthcare IT systems, which could open the market further to new entrants.
- AI-powered clinical workflow agents and generative AI now capture roughly **48% of European health venture capital**, with HealthTech leading all European sectors by capturing **21.8% (€5.2 billion)** of total venture investment in September 2026.
- Business Sweden signed a **Memorandum of Understanding with Northwell Health** (US) on November 4, 2026, to support Swedish healthcare innovation companies expanding internationally.

*Note: A comprehensive list of every health tech company that entered the Swedish market in 2026 is not available from a single source. The above reflects the most prominent entries, funding rounds, and expansions reported as of mid-November 2026.*

context.content:
Developing the full concept behind Neko Health took years. For a long time, the company struggled to deliver a functional prototype to investors, as they worked to balance the demands of hardware, software, AI and clinical results. By 2023, they had developed an initial offering consisting of a rapid, noninvasive body scan with cardiovascular measurements, skin assessments, blood testing and an in-person consultation with a doctor. They rolled this out in Stockholm, Sweden, before setting their sights abroad. Neko expanded into the United Kingdom in 2024, and just recently opened a brick-and-mortar office in NYC in 2026.

## The scan experience: What it is and how it works [...] If you’re one of the millions of Americans who lack comprehensive healthcare, a full-body scan may sound completely out of reach. CT scans, PET scans and MRI imaging are generally reserved for those with severe medical ailments, or those with the financial capital to prioritize health and wellness, without worrying about making the rent. But what if you could circumvent those hurdles and get a clear picture of your own health, including warning signs of disease, before you even develop any symptoms? That’s the promise behind Neko Health, a Swedish tech startup that boasts a controversial AI-powered body scanning technique. Co-founded by Spotify CEO Daniel Ek and entrepreneur Hjalmar Nilsonne, the company officially opened its first U.S. clinic in New York City in September 2026, offering [...] ## How did Neko Health start?

According to a company press release, Neko Health was originally founded back in 2018. As the story goes, Spotify CEO Daniel Ek was interested in partnering with Swedish entrepreneur Hjalmar Nilsonne after seeing the latter’s work in artificial intelligence. Ek reached out via Twitter, sparking a discussion surrounding the pitfalls of the modern healthcare system. At the time, Nilsonne was winding down an energy startup, while Ek was looking for a challenge that could make a meaningful contribution to society. Though neither partner has a formal background in medicine, the duo managed to create and scale their vision, thanks in part to Nilsonne’s engineering background and Ek’s executive prowess and tech connections.

 AI Captures Nearly Half of HealthTech VC: Sector analyses published this week highlight that generative AI,clinical workflow agents, and biological foundation models ("world models for biology" using automated wet labs) now account for roughly 48% of European health venture capital. [...] Milestone-Driven MedTech M&A: Dealmaking advisors tracking European device transactions in early November noted that strategic acquirers are relying heavily on post-CE-mark and reimbursement-linked earn-outs to bridge valuation gaps while targeting commercial-stage continuous diagnostics and procedural devices.

With new mandates around the European Health Data Space (EHDS) in 2027, there is now an interoperability challenge.

  

The real challenge isn’t getting systems to connect technically, but getting them to agree on what the data means, according to Annemieke Ålenius, the Deputy Director General at Swedish eHealth Agency, and AI Expert at AI Sweden.

  

The EHDS is a harmonised framework governing the processing, access, exchange, and secondary use of electronic health data in the European Union (EU).

  

Ålenius’ agency is tasked to set up the national digital infrastructure and services, allowing healthcare professionals to access medication information across regions. [...] “This takes place at the same time as human resources are diminishing and demands for care are growing,” she adds.

  

The same system integration challenge is also shared among the Nordic countries.

  

The Nordic AI Health Map, a large-scale collaborative mapping across publicly funded healthcare in the Nordic region, has identified more than 800 healthcare AI initiatives, but only one-third have reached routine use.

  

Hence, countries are working on data integration and exchanging knowledge through channels such as the Nordic Council of Ministers’ eHealth Group.

  

Other challenges include cybersecurity issues in remote care and developing evidence-based treatments with AI. [...] HealthcareData
